subject: dust mites in bedding
title: What If You Never Washed Your Bedsheets?

scenes.text: What if you never washed your bedsheets? You'd never sleep alone again. Something would move in.
Every day you shed around a gram of dead skin, and your bed collects it every night.
scenes.keywords: bed sheets close up morning light

scenes.text: That skin feeds house dust mites. Four in five American homes have their allergen in at least one bed.
Each female lays dozens of eggs, and in about a month those eggs grow into breeding adults.
Adults live for up to a few months, feeding, breeding and leaving waste in the fabric.
The sneezing isn't caused by the mites. It's their droppings and dead bodies, piling up in sheets you never washed.

first_comment: Dust mites don't even drink: they soak up water from humid air, which is why damp bedrooms suit them best. What everyday thing should we never do next?
